what_happened: The operator asked for a speed change: cut A would open its pull request early, "when verification starts". The operator did not check the order of stages first. Athena's own checks take about 12 minutes and run before verification. CI therefore got only about 2 minutes' head start on a 16-minute run. The first landing after cut A (PR #180) still took 18 minutes. The operator had already put this wording into job 20261025-055626-er96 and its retries.
cause: Athena has no recorded, current timeline of its stages (producer, checks, verifier, landing) with measured durations. A request that sets a timing change is therefore written from an assumed stage order. Neither the request intake nor the reading compares a latency claim against measured stage data, so the expected gain is never estimated before work is spent. The error shows up only after the change lands, in real timings.
prevention: Add a default, shown to whoever writes or reads a speed request: before requesting or accepting a timing change, write down the measured stage timeline (producer, checks, verifier, landing, with durations from recent jobs). Then state the expected saving from that timeline. For cut A the timeline would have shown that "when verification starts" saves only about 2 minutes, and that opening the pull request when the checks start would have saved about 14.
proposed_request: Make cut A's early pull request open when Athena's own checks start (the roughly 12-minute stage that runs before verification), not when verification starts, so CI overlaps the checks. First, from recent jobs, record the measured stage timeline (producer, checks, verifier, landing) and state the expected saving. Acceptance: (1) the early pull request opens at the start of the checks stage; (2) a test shows the open event comes before the checks run, using the real stage order; (3) the first landing after the change finishes at least 10 minutes sooner than the 18-minute PR #180 baseline, or the shortfall is explained from the timeline; (4) if the checks fail, the early pull request is closed or marked so that it cannot land.
